DiagnosticWarnings: 1 monologue turn(s) exceed 35 words without action line splits.

DisqualifyingFlags: grok-4.5: Protagonist cued as PETER from the opening (and throughout) despite the book withholding the name until the final line; must remain NARRATOR until the source reveal
grok-4.5: Speaking supporting role cued as bare BOYFRIEND (relational/unstable label forbidden by closed-cast rules)
grok-4: Missing explicit sound cue in multiple scenes
grok-4: Inconsistent character visual restatement across time jumps
grok-4: Some action lines contain unfilmable internal states

SelfBiasNotes: ⚠️ grok-4.5 rated its own screenplay 8.2/10 vs. a 6.8/10 average from 1 other judge(s) (+1.4) — possible self-preference bias.

grok-4.5.grok-4.5: Strong visual locking via title-page Notes and consistent re-entry traits for the core four; solid short-clip action and near-complete sound coverage. Fidelity suffers from premature naming of the narrator, compression that drops several mid-book confrontations (early slap, full doctor/ER setup, Nick's wrecked apartment), and the illegal BOYFRIEND cue. Pacing is tight with effective Seattle bookends but loses some escalation density around the crash and stabbing. Dialogue stays close to book cadence when present. Production-blocked by the two hard cast/reveal violations.
grok-4.5.gpt-5.6-terra: Highest fidelity: correctly keeps NARRATOR until the final 'President Peter Olson' line, covers more source beats (doctor visit, battlefield dream, early slap fight, Nick apartment mess, Trans Am crash visual, full stabbing aftermath), and invents only light stable names (DAVID, ELLEN, HARRIS) for unnamed speakers. Directibility is concrete and clip-friendly; pacing escalates cleanly through the accident/stabbing/prison arc with good Seattle coda. Dialogue preserves book wording and subtext in short turns. Sound cues are present and specific in every scene. Character looks are described on first entry and some re-entries but lack a locked upfront bible and occasional restatement after time jumps, the only real softness.

grok-4.gpt-5.6-terra: Strong fidelity to source beats and dialogue, consistent character visuals across time jumps, concrete filmable actions, and explicit sound cues in every scene.
grok-4.grok-4.5: Covers core beats but drops several source details, has weaker character consistency, and omits required audio cues in several scenes.

JudgeSummaries.grok-4.5: Strongest: Screenplay B because it alone obeys the narrator-name reveal rule, covers more essential source confrontations and the crash without major drops, and stays production-ready. Weakest: Screenplay A because the early PETER naming and illegal BOYFRIEND cue are hard closed-cast/fidelity violations that block greenlight despite superior visual locking.
JudgeSummaries.grok-4: Strongest: Screenplay A because it maintains source fidelity, consistent visuals, and required audio cues across every scene. Weakest: Screenplay B because it omits required sound cues and has inconsistent character descriptions across time periods.
